editorial.headline: Corporate Training, With a Clear Bali Caveat
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers company-run job training across practical, professional and personal-development subjects, with full foreign ownership nationally and an address-sensitive Bali position.
editorial.body:
Corporate training under this activity is broad by design, but not vague. It covers company-run job training in areas including training methodology, occupational health and safety, motivation, personal development, career development and neuro-linguistic programming, alongside other training subjects delivered by a company. The unifying idea is practical learning organised as a business activity: training intended to build capability, confidence or professional direction.

The record identifies companies as the organisers of the training. It does not list any registration scales for this activity, so the classification should not be stretched into assumptions about the size of operator it is designed for. What is clear is the subject range: it can accommodate both technical workplace learning and programmes centred on individual development, provided the training is conducted by a company.

Nationally, the position is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That makes the national rule unusually straightforward: the record places no lower foreign-equity cap on this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires a more exact reading. This activity is marked **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and is not blocked by the province-wide moratorium that applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA. Its stated Bali position is medium-high or high risk, with verification required for the specific address. In other words, Bali is not a blanket prohibition here, but neither is it a conclusion to reach without checking the location at which the training business will operate.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali is not a blanket prohibition here, but the operating address still needs verification.
